title: A Functional Representation of Credit Behavior for Probability of Default Modeling
abstract: arXiv:2610.07888v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This paper proposes a framework for modeling probability of default via functional data analysis. By representing a series of credit variables as functions, we investigate whether intra-monthly information improves default predictability in linear models. We further show how a range of widely used variables, among them available funds, utilization rate, and overdraft, can all be derived from three quantities observed over time. Namely, 1) the type of each account, 2) the balance of the account, and 3) the size of the credit limit on the account. Retaining these quantities as continuous-time processes, rather than reducing them to monthly aggregated values, yields a continuous faithful representation of the borrower. translated_title: 用于违约概率建模的信用行为函数表示
translated_abstract: 本文提出了一个通过函数数据分析对违约概率进行建模的框架。通过将一系列信用变量表示为函数，我们研究了月内信息是否能改善线性模型中的违约预测能力。我们进一步展示了广泛使用的一系列变量，包括可用资金、使用率和透支额，都可以从随时间观测的三个量中推导出来，即：1) 每个账户的类型，2) 账户的余额，以及 3) 账户的信用额度大小。将这些量保持为连续时间过程，而不是将其简化为月度汇总值，可以得到对借款人连续且忠实的表示。在分析这三个过程时，我们发现与银行工作日顺序位置相关的重复事件产生了强烈的周期性模式。因此，我们开发了一个相对时间框架来对齐这些周期性模式（摘要原文在此处截断）。
tldr: 本文提出基于函数数据分析的违约概率建模框架，将账户类型、余额和信用额度表示为连续时间函数过程，从而推导出可用资金、使用率、透支等常用变量，并发现银行工作日相关的周期性模式与月内信息能够改善线性模型的违约预测能力。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a functional data analysis framework for probability of default modeling, representing account type, balance, and credit limit as continuous-time processes from which common credit variables can be derived, showing that intra-monthly information and cyclical banking-day patterns improve default predictability in linear models.
